novelty.method: curated modern exclusion list: approved-drug compounds (n=30), extensively-studied natural-product leads (n=38), graph-level modern evidence (grade A/B or modern-tradition use), and a curated literature-familiarity prior (n=113 species). No offline ChEMBL target-annotation check is available, so novelty scores are upper bounds.
novelty.basis: curated exclusion list + graph modern evidence

mechanism.rationale: A heterogeneous class — receptor prediction is class-level only. Many are potently toxic (Aconitum, Veratrum, Datura, Papaver) and dose-critical; this system never proposes dosing.

candidates.asian_theory_justification: 四氣五味: 寒, 苦. 歸經: 心/脾/胃/肝/胆/大肠. The classical prediction is that a 寒 苦 drug entering the 心/脾/胃/肝/胆/大肠 channel reaches intestine-related patterns. Chemotype alkaloid. This is a theory-generated prediction, not evidence: it is tested against chemistry and target biology in eval/report.json → drug_discovery.theory_predictivity.

development_path.kind: reproducible sub-micromolar target engagement in two orthogonal assays, selectivity over the closest paralogue, and measurable exposure without the structural alerts above

residual_risk: no structural red flag from the heuristic filter; safety data still pending

drivers: novelty 0.03 ± 0.18 is the largest uncertainty driver
plausibility 0.83 ± 0.18 is the largest uncertainty driver
uncertainty.notes: composite_ci is a 95% interval from Monte-Carlo propagation of the factor uncertainties (triangular distribution, seed 0); it is not an experimental confidence interval.

falsification.experiment: Enzyme- or cell-based dose–response for opioid receptor with the candidate compound and a reference inhibitor; confirm target engagement by a second orthogonal assay.
falsification.expected_if_true: Reproducible, concentration-dependent target engagement in two orthogonal assays.
falsification.kill_criteria: No engagement below the compound's solubility limit, or activity only in one assay (assay artefact) → the candidate is dead.

safety.notes: Research use only. Not medical advice; no dose or human-use protocol is given. The lead plant is excluded from the toxicological class list for this candidate.
